title: Model call ledger
summary: Capture and price individual model responses, link them to their work, and make the evidence available in Studio and Magazine.

openDecisions.title: Storage
openDecisions.question: Which store should own the call ledger?

options.A: Task Server SQLite with a host outbox

openDecisions.recommendation: A. Task Server SQLite with a host outbox
openDecisions.rationale: One Task Server needs durable writes and arbitrary pivots at modest ingest rate. Use one local data volume and migrate when active multi-node writes or measured operational limits require it.

openDecisions.title: Delivery durability
openDecisions.question: How do hosts deliver usage during an outage?
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Persistent outbox and durable ACK
openDecisions.rationale: Persist before advancing the reader, replay after reconnect, and signal any coverage gaps.

openDecisions.title: Cost display
openDecisions.question: What values does the product store and display?

options.A: Dated list rates alongside attributable provider points

openDecisions.recommendation: A. Dated list rates alongside attributable provider points
openDecisions.rationale: Store resolved components and basis. Store recorded comparable points only where a provider reports and attributes them.

openDecisions.title: Retention
openDecisions.question: How long are individual calls retained?
openDecisions.recommendation: A. 180 days plus durable privacy-minimized rollups
openDecisions.rationale: Balances detail for comparisons and diagnostics against volume and personal data.

openDecisions.title: Finding attribution
openDecisions.question: How is the cost of a multi-finding round assigned?

options.A: Explicit primary plus a shared bucket

openDecisions.recommendation: A. Explicit primary plus a shared bucket
openDecisions.rationale: Preserves additive rankings and links every co-trigger in detail.

openDecisions.title: Presentation
openDecisions.question: Which reporting surfaces are product defaults?

options.A: Explorer, fixed pipeline and lifecycle, and daily/weekly Magazine

openDecisions.recommendation: A. Explorer, fixed pipeline and lifecycle, and daily/weekly Magazine
openDecisions.rationale: Start with the measured night in product; promote interaction and issues on the same query contracts.

openDecisions.title: Backfill
openDecisions.question: How much history should be reconciled first?
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Measured night then audited 30 days
openDecisions.rationale: Fast proof with exact coverage, then a bounded comparison against existing reports.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Coding night in Model Calls

Read AGENTS.md, docs/model-call-ledger/index.html and docs/system/domains/tokens.md and token-pricing.md. Apply the Dossier recommendations for storage, backfill and presentation unless a recorded owner decision selects another option. Record the option implemented in the card results.

## Scope
Task Server ledger and in-product read path.

Create the portable call/coverage schema and the separate SQLite store. Add an authenticated operator-only historical import/ingest path. Use the Codex source records for the 27 Nov 21:52 to 28 Nov 09:12:07 UTC measurement, and fall back to AGT-4375 calls.csv and measurements.json from its card results when source IDs are unavailable. Use the validated dataset fingerprint and card/run/response ordinal identity in the import namespace. Keep the response ID alias path available for later evidence. Stay in an authorized workspace, and import only sanitized usage and bounded metadata. Capture usage basis and timestamp basis; keep gaps nullable. Use the existing ITokenPricing seam when a historical tariff is supported, and expose explicit unpriced coverage otherwise.
Expose a scoped time-window query and response detail route. Under Token Usage add a Model Calls entry that shows total calls and tokens and supports a card filter, run expansion and response detail. Show happened-at, observed/inferred provenance, tokens, list-price status and any fields known. Link to the source card evidence under normal permission checks. Preserve legacy pricing and admission unchanged. Use the Dossier prototype as visual direction.

## Acceptance
- Importing the reference export yields 19,774 coding responses on 58 cards, 2,639,640,822 tokens, 4,592 waits and 924 status checks; 680 research responses are outside this coding proof.
- Repeat the same import, restart the server and prove counts and IDs are unchanged. A late usage revision cannot create a new response.
- An isolated permitted workspace Time window → card → run → response drill works in Playwright and a different project cannot read aggregates or any individual call. Capture the proof in light and dark.
- Publish comparison against the reference totals with unknown fields and price coverage. Do not require USD 765 equality across incompatible or unresolved tariff evidence.

Record the scoped storage decision against ADR-0063. Inspect the existing studio_token_usage ingest before choosing the compatibility path. Preserve its run-level contract and make the response store authoritative only for the new routes.
